name: Uejima Onitsura
credit: Portrait of Uejima Onitsura · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Uejima Onitsura (1661–1738) was a haikai poet of Itami, near Osaka, sometimes called the Bashō of the west. He held that there is no haikai outside sincerity (makoto), and he worked out much the same conclusions as Bashō independently.
These are the hokku that Basil Hall Chamberlain attributes to him in Bashō and the Japanese Poetical Epigram (1902), each with Chamberlain's rhymed English rendering.

poems.title: Mono-sugo ya
poems.author: Uejima Onitsura
poems.text:
Mono-sugo ya
Ara omoshiro no
Kaeri-bana

poems.title: Natsu wa mata
poems.author: Uejima Onitsura
poems.text:
Natsu wa mata
Fuyu ga mashi ja to
Iware-keri

poems.title: Nyoppori to
poems.author: Uejima Onitsura
poems.text:
Nyoppori to
Aki no sora naru
Fuji no yama

poems.title: Gaikotsu no
poems.author: Uejima Onitsura
poems.text:
Gaikotsu no
Ue wa yosōte
Hana-mi kana

poems.title: Mata hitotsu
poems.author: Uejima Onitsura
poems.text:
Mata hitotsu
Hana ni tsure-yuku
Inochi kana

poems.title: Saku kara ni
poems.author: Uejima Onitsura
poems.text:
Saku kara ni
Miru kara ni hana no
Chiru kara ni

poems.title: Mono-sugo ya
poems.author: Uejima Onitsura
poems.text:
Uncanny and yet pleasing are
These flow'rs that blossom out of time.

poems.title: Natsu wa mata
poems.author: Uejima Onitsura
poems.text:
And in the summer, folks opined
That winter was to be preferred,

poems.title: Nyoppori to
poems.author: Uejima Onitsura
poems.text:
Without a word of warning, there,
In th' autumn sky, Mount Fuji stands.

poems.title: Gaikotsu no
poems.author: Uejima Onitsura
poems.text:
Oh! flower-gazers, who have decked
The surface of their skeletons!

poems.title: Mata hitotsu
poems.author: Uejima Onitsura
poems.text:
Together with one blossom more,
Oh! life, thou goest on thy way.

poems.title: Saku kara ni
poems.author: Uejima Onitsura
poems.text:
They blossom forth, and so I gaze,
And so these flowers fade, and so.......
